answer:
Use FEniCS legacy (dolfin) to solve a 2D plane-stress small-strain linear elasticity problem on a parallelogram domain.
The geometry is a parallelogram with vertices (0,0), (1,0), (1.2,0.3), (0.2,0.3), with unit thickness.
The material is isotropic with E=70e9 Pa, ν=0.33, ρ=2700 kg/m³, and gravity g=9.81 m/s² acting in the -y direction as a distributed body force (ρ·g ≈ 26487 N/m³ in -y) over the whole domain.
Use the reduced plane-stress constitutive law (effective Lamé parameters derived for plane stress with unit thickness).
Mesh the domain with a structured grid of 72 first-order (P1) Lagrange triangles, arranged so that a mesh node lands exactly on the load point (1.1, 0.15).
For example, use a structured parallelogram triangulation with an even number of segments (e.g. 6) along each inclined edge so that (1.1, 0.15), the midpoint of the right edge from (1,0) to (1.2,0.3), coincides exactly with a mesh vertex; document the chosen mesh layout.
Use the vector displacement space VectorFunctionSpace(mesh, "Lagrange", 1, dim=2).
Clamp the left inclined edge, the segment from (0,0) to (0.2,0.3) lying on the line y = 1.5x, by fixing both displacement components (u = v = 0).
Apply the horizontal point load as a PointSource on the x-component of the displacement space: PointSource(V.sub(0), Point(1.1, 0.15), -5000.0), i.e. -5000 N in the negative x-direction, not as a smeared boundary load.
Assemble the plane-stress variational form and solve the resulting linear system with a direct linear solver (e.g. "mumps" or default LU).
Compute the in-plane Cauchy stress field from the displacement solution using the plane-stress constitutive relation.
Compute the von Mises stress from the in-plane Cauchy stress components and project it onto a scalar P1 function space via project(..., FunctionSpace(mesh, "P", 1)).
Save both the displacement field u and the von Mises field sigma_vM to XDMF files for ParaView visualization.
Print a numerical summary to console: maximum absolute displacement (from u.vector().get_local()), maximum von Mises stress, and their min/max values for sanity checking.
Note that the von Mises maximum will be localized at the load point (1.1, 0.15) due to the point-load singularity in a P1 mesh; this is expected behavior.
